slides.h: Diagnosed with osteoporosis? Wondering if you can still do Pilates?
body: Short answer: yes, with a few changes. Swipe.
Osteoporosis means your bones have become thinner and more fragile, so they break more easily.
It usually has no symptoms. Many people only find out after a bone density scan, or a fracture.
Exercise is recommended for people with osteoporosis, especially strength, balance and posture work.
Bones respond to load, and stronger muscles and better balance help you stay steady on your feet. Check in with your GP or physio first.

slides.h: Some moves come out. Others come in.
body: We leave out loaded forward bending, like roll-ups and crunches, and deep twisting under load. Those put extra pressure on the front of the spine.
Your instructor swaps them for options that suit you.

list: springs and straps for legs, hips and back
upper back strength and spinal extension

body: Message us before your free intro class. Share your diagnosis and any advice from your doctor or physio, and your instructor can adjust from day one.
